12	version, and stops you from inventing APIs — match the installed versions and
13	follow the ecosystem catalog instead of guessing.

34	vs `date-utils`, …) and picking the wrong one is the #1 failure.

37	its top **first**: it opens with a task → package decision table that settles the
38	common cases (landing page, dashboard, data grid, calendar, charts, editor, app
39	shell, i18n), followed by the ecosystem catalog with a one-line "what it's for /
40	what to use instead" per package for everything else. Use it to choose the

71	      before moving online. Batch all uncertain symbol lookups for that package.

75	      latest minor of that major — it tracks the major but not the exact patch.
76	      Use it when LOCAL has no docs for the package.

104	   confirmed installed in Step 1.** Import from those packages exactly — do
105	   not substitute look-alike libraries (MUI, Ant, plain `<input>`) and do not
106	   reach for a `@gravity-ui/*` package that Step 1 did not confirm installed.
107	   Follow the prop APIs from the docs you just read, not memory; if a prop
108	   you want is not documented, it does not exist — use the documented one, or
109	   ask the user.

112	   writing: typography variants, the flex contract, theming/ladders,
113	   `Button view`, `Icon data`. Per-component traps live in the package's own
114	   `dist/docs`.

117	   (typically `tsc --noEmit`; for monorepos, the workspace's typecheck script).
118	   Fix every error before reporting completion — a type error almost always
119	   means a wrong/invented prop, a wrong import path, or a version mismatch,
120	   which is precisely what Steps 0–1 were meant to prevent.
121	
122	   - If the typecheck surfaces a prop/path that contradicts the docs you read
123	     in Step 1, trust the **installed version** (the typechecker), not the
124	     docs snapshot — the docs may be from a different minor. Re-ground: read
125	     the package's `dist/docs/INDEX.md` in `node_modules` for the exact
126	     installed types.
127	   - If the typecheck is unavailable (no TS in the project), say so
128	     explicitly and ask the user how they want to verify; do not silently
129	     skip verification.
130	   - **Escape hatch.** If the user explicitly waived verification ("just
131	     sketch it", "quick prototype", "no need to check"), you may skip the
132	     typecheck — but state this plainly in your reply: *"typecheck skipped by
133	     user request — code is not verified"*. Do not skip silently.
134	   - **Know what typecheck does not cover.** A green `tsc` proves the API is
135	     real; it says nothing about layout or contrast. Before reporting done,
136	     say so, and either check or list for the user to check by hand: the
137	     screen in both `light` and `dark` themes (text and controls on colored
138	     fills especially), narrow (~375px) and wide (~1400px) viewports for
139	     horizontal overflow, and empty / loading / error states.
140	
141	## Hard rules
142	
143	- **`@gravity-ui/uikit` MUST be installed in every Gravity UI project.** It is
144	  the base component + design-token library every other `@gravity-ui/*` package
145	  builds on; without it components render unstyled. If `package.json` lacks it,
146	  stop and have the user install and configure it first (setup:
147	  `https://gravity-ui.com/llms/uikit/llms.txt`).
148	- **Read `package.json` before importing any `@gravity-ui/*` package.** Never
149	  assume a package is installed; never assume its major version.
150	- **Do not invent props or components.** Before using a component API you are
151	  not 100% sure of, check `rules/hallucination-traps.md` (ecosystem patterns)
152	  and the component's README in `dist/docs`. If still unsure, ask the user
153	  rather than guessing.
154	- **Never guess icon names** — they are hallucinated more often than not. To
155	  match an icon from a screenshot/photo/mock, run `scripts/icon-image-search.sh`
156	  (reverse image search). With only a description, look the name up on
157	  `gravity-ui.com/icons` or ask the user — do not invent one. Then pass it as an
158	  object (`<Icon data={CheckIcon} />`), never a string key. See
159	  `references/icons.md`.
160	- **Theming uses semantic `--g-*` tokens.** Never hardcode colors (`#fff`,
161	  `blue-500`); never hand-write `dark:` overrides. Full token tables live in
162	  `references/theming.md`; the cross-cutting traps (partial brand overrides,
163	  a `ThemeProvider` that themes the whole page, controls on a brand background) live in
164	  `rules/hallucination-traps.md`.
165	- **Required setup is package-specific** (style imports, `ThemeProvider`,
166	  peer-deps). It lives in each package's root README under "Required setup" —
167	  read it once per package, do not rely on memory.
168

172	already implied by the rules above; this section exists as an explicit
173	stop-sign. If you are about to do any of these, stop and re-ground.
174

176	  `<input>`/`<button>`, or look-alike component libs. Use the `@gravity-ui/*`
177	  package the task needs.
178	- **Do not invent component APIs or props.** If a prop is not in the docs you
179	  read in Step 1, it does not exist — do not write `variant=`, `color=`,
180	  `name=` (on `Icon`), or a `header-3` variant. Use the documented prop or
181	  ask the user. See `rules/hallucination-traps.md`.
182	- **Do not use the `/llms/<pkg>/llms.txt` "latest" alias as a fallback.** It
183	  serves the newest major, which may differ from the installed one and have a
184	  different API. The versioned online fallback is the major-line URL
185	  (`/llms/<pkg>/<major>/llms.txt`); below that, go LOCAL.
186	- **Do not partial-brand.** Setting only `--g-color-base-brand` leaves
187	  selection, focus, links and contrast on the default accent — a mismatched
188	  UI. Override the full brand token set, on each theme you support.
189	- **Do not override internal markup with `[class*='…']` / ID selectors.**
190	  That's written against one DOM structure and breaks silently when the
191	  component changes. Climb the customization ladder
192	  (global token → component CSS API → narrow flagged hack) before ever
193	  touching structure.
194

196	
197	These files live alongside this SKILL.md and load only when relevant:
198	
199	- `references/package-routing.md` — offline snapshot of the ecosystem catalog
200	  (`gravity-ui.com/llms.txt`), refreshed each skill release. Used as the
201	  offline fallback in Step 0.
202	- `references/theming.md` — verbatim copy of uikit's `docs/theming.md`:
203	  `--g-*` token layers, `ThemeProvider`, branding, custom themes, scoped
204	  themes, `uikit-themer`. The bundled copy may lag — read
205	  `node_modules/@gravity-ui/uikit/build/docs/guides/theming.md` for the
206	  version-matched file.
207	- `references/layout.md` — verbatim copy of uikit's `docs/layout.md`:
208	  spacing scale (`--g-spacing-*`), `Flex`/`Box`, `Row`/`Col`/`Container`
209	  grid, breakpoints, `useLayoutContext`.
210	- `references/icons.md` — finding an icon by image
211	  (`scripts/icon-image-search.sh`) or on gravity-ui.com/icons; the
212	  object-vs-string rendering rule.
213	- `rules/hallucination-traps.md` — Incorrect/Correct pairs for the most
214	  commonly invented APIs: typography variants (`header-3..6` don't exist, no
215	  `Heading`), the flex contract (`min-width:0`, who shrinks), theming traps
216	  (partial brand overrides, a `ThemeProvider` that themes the whole page, customization
217	  ladder), `Button view` not `variant`, `Icon data` not `name`. Per-component
218	  traps live in each package's `dist/docs`, not here.

# @gravity-ui/charts documentation Documentation for the **installed** version of `@gravity-ui/charts`. Your training data may be outdated — these files are the source of truth. Paths are relative to this file (`node_modules/@gravity-ui/charts/dist/docs/`). ## For AI agents A declarative React charting library for Gravity UI apps — render line, area, bar, pie, scatter, treemap, and other charts from a single `data` config, themed to match the rest of the app. ### When to use - Standard business charts: `line`, `area`, `bar-x`/`bar-y`, `pie`, `scatter`, `treemap`, `waterfall`, `sankey`, `radar`, `heatmap`, `funnel`, `x-range`. - Visualizations that must follow Gravity UI theming (light/dark) and share tokens with a `@gravity-ui/uikit` app. - Rendering a chart from declarative data rather than drawing imperatively. ### When not to use - Projects still on `@gravity-ui/chartkit` — that is the older adapter-based wrapper (YAGR/Highcharts/D3); this package is the modern standalone renderer and is not a drop-in replacement. - Plain tabular data — use [`@gravity-ui/table`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/table). - Non-React or server-only rendering — `Chart` renders React SVG and needs the DOM. ### Common pitfalls - **The component is `Chart`, not `ChartKit`.** Import `{Chart}` from `@gravity-ui/charts`; `ChartKit` belongs to the separate legacy `@gravity-ui/chartkit` package. - **The data prop is `data`, shaped `{series: {data: [...]}}`.** Each entry in `series.data` is one series with its own `type` and `data` array — there is no top-level array of series. - **Nothing renders without a sized container.** `Chart` fills its parent, so give the wrapper an explicit height. - **Requires uikit setup.** Wrap in `ThemeProvider` and import `@gravity-ui/uikit/styles/styles.css`; `@gravity-ui/uikit` is a required peer dependency. ### Useful docs - [Get started](./get-started.md) - [Theming](./guides/theming.md) - [Tooltip](./guides/tooltip.md) - [Legend](./guides/legend.md) - [HTML Content](./guides/html.md) - [Value Formatting](./guides/value-formatting.md) - [Data Labels](./guides/data-labels.md) - [Axis Types](./guides/axes/axis-types.md) - [Axis Labels](./guides/axes/axis-labels.md) ## Install ```shell npm install @gravity-ui/uikit @gravity-ui/charts ``` `@gravity-ui/uikit` is a required peer dependency — it provides the theming and styles the charts rely on. ## Usage Import the `@gravity-ui/uikit` styles once in your entry point, wrap your app in `ThemeProvider`, and render a `Chart` inside a container with an explicit height: ```tsx import {ThemeProvider} from '@gravity-ui/uikit'; import {Chart} from '@gravity-ui/charts'; import '@gravity-ui/uikit/styles/fonts.css'; import '@gravity-ui/uikit/styles/styles.css'; const data = { series: { data: [ { type: 'line', name: 'Temperature', data: [ {x: 0, y: 10}, {x: 1, y: 25}, {x: 2, y: 18}, {x: 3, y: 30}, ], }, ], }, }; export default function App() { return (
); } ``` `Chart` adapts to its parent's size, so the wrapping element must have a height. ## Guides - [Adding a series plugin](./development/adding-series-plugin.md) — This checklist is for contributors adding a built-in series plugin to Charts. - [Area range series](./guides/series-types/area-range.md) — An area range series fills the interval between a lower and an upper value at each X position. - [Area series](./guides/series-types/area.md) — An area series fills the space between a line and its baseline. - [Axes](./guides/axes/index.md) — Configure the X axis with xAxis and Y axes with yAxis. ## Theming
### Styles + fonts are required; order matters
❌ **Incorrect** — missing imports, or theme before base:
```tsx
import './theme.css';                                  // before styles.css → gets overwritten
import {ThemeProvider} from '@gravity-ui/uikit';
// no styles.css, no fonts.css → components render unstyled
```
✓ **Correct**:
```tsx
import '@gravity-ui/uikit/styles/fonts.css';           // fonts first
import '@gravity-ui/uikit/styles/styles.css';          // then base
import './theme.css';                                  // custom ALWAYS after styles.css
import {ThemeProvider} from '@gravity-ui/uikit';
```
**Why:** without `styles.css` + `fonts.css` imported once at the entry point,
every component renders unstyled. A custom theme file imported *before*
`styles.css` is overwritten by it in the cascade — custom always comes after.
### `theme` takes five values — no `"default"` or `"auto"`
❌ `<ThemeProvider theme="default">`
❌ `<ThemeProvider theme="auto">`
✓ `<ThemeProvider theme="light">` / `"dark"` / `"light-hc"` / `"dark-hc"`
✓ `<ThemeProvider theme="system">` (resolves to light/dark from OS preference)
### Branding means a full token set, on both themes — never 2–4 tokens
❌ **Incorrect** — partial override:
```css
.g-root { --g-color-base-brand: #007AFF; }
```
✓ **Correct** — override the full brand group, per theme:
```css
.g-root_theme_light {
  --g-color-base-brand: #007AFF;
  --g-color-base-brand-hover: #0066D6;
  --g-color-base-selection: rgba(0, 122, 255, 0.05);
  --g-color-base-selection-hover: rgba(0, 122, 255, 0.1);
  --g-color-line-brand: #007AFF;
  --g-color-text-brand: #007AFF;
  --g-color-text-brand-contrast: #FFFFFF;   /* required: text on brand bg */
  --g-color-text-link: #007AFF;
  --g-color-text-link-hover: #0066D6;
}
.g-root_theme_dark {
  /* different values — dark usually needs a brighter brand */
  --g-color-base-brand: #2E8BFF;
  /* … same set, dark-tuned … */
}
```
**Why:** the semantic layer has many tokens pointing at "brand" — selection,
focus, links, the contrast text on a brand background. Override only
`--g-color-base-brand` and you get a UI where the button is branded but
selection, links and focus rings are still the default accent. Provide the full
set, and provide it for *each* theme you support (dark themes usually need a
brighter brand than light). Forgetting `--g-color-text-brand-contrast` makes
text on a brand button unreadable.
Better than hand-writing: generate the full set with the
[Themer](https://gravity-ui.com/themer) web tool or
[`@gravity-ui/uikit-themer`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit-themer) — both
recalculate the dependent palette from a single base color.
### A section `ThemeProvider` with no provider above it themes the whole page
❌ **Incorrect** — a dark widget mounted where no `ThemeProvider` (or v8
`Provider`) wraps it: an embedded widget, a micro-frontend, a separate React
root:
```tsx
<ThemeProvider theme="dark">   {/* no provider above → writes to document.body */}
  <Toolbar />
</ThemeProvider>
```
✓ **Correct**:
```tsx
<ThemeProvider scoped theme="dark">
  <Toolbar />
</ThemeProvider>
```
**Why:** only the outermost `ThemeProvider` writes the theme class to
`document.body` — globally, last-wins. One nested inside another
`ThemeProvider` (or a v8 `Provider`) is always scoped, with or without the prop,
so a dark section inside the app needs no `scoped`. With no provider above,
`scoped` renders a dedicated `<div class="g-root g-root_theme_dark">` around the
children *and* updates the theme React context (so `useTheme` inside the
section sees the section's theme). For a CSS-only region without context, apply
the class manually: `<div className={getRootClassName({theme: 'dark'})}>`.
### Controls on a brand/colored background: fixed contrast, both themes
❌ **Incorrect** — default button on a brand-colored hero:
```tsx
<section style={{background: 'var(--g-color-base-brand)'}}>
  <Button>Sign up</Button>   {/* default view follows theme → low contrast on bright bg */}
</section>
```
✓ **Correct** — use a `*-contrast` view, which is built for a contrast
background, or scope a CSS override fixing contrast for both themes:
```tsx
<section style={{background: 'var(--g-color-base-brand)'}}>
  <Button view="normal-contrast">Sign up</Button>   {/* also outlined-contrast, flat-contrast */}
</section>
```
**Why:** a brand-colored fill is usually the *same* color in light and dark
(it's a fill, not a themed surface), so the control on top should keep a fixed
contrast in both themes rather than lightening/darkening with the theme.
`normal-contrast` / `outlined-contrast` / `flat-contrast` do exactly that.
Do **not** reach for `raised` here — its surface is themed (light in light,
dark in dark), so it does not hold contrast on a fixed fill. If no `*-contrast`
view fits, override the component's CSS API (`--g-button-background-color`,
`--g-button-text-color`, …) scoped to the section, with contrast values for
both themes. This is distinct from `--g-color-text-brand-contrast`, which is
about text on a *brand button* (`view="action"`).
### Customization ladder — descend only when there's no higher handle
When you need to change how a Gravity UI component looks, try in this order:
1. **Global tokens** (`--g-*` semantic tokens / theme) — change the look
   everywhere by changing the token, not components one by one.
2. **Component's own CSS API** (`--g-button-*`, `--g-card-border-radius`,
   `--g-text-input-*`, …) — scoped to the wrapper / class of the spot you're
   changing. Check the component's README for the variables it exposes.
3. **A narrow, flagged hack** — a custom class on a specific internal element,
   with a comment "hack on internal classes, pinned to version <X>", and a note
   to upstream it. Only after confirming step 1 and 2 don't expose a handle.
4. **NEVER** broad structural matches: `[class*='…']` or ID selectors against
   internal markup. Such an override is written against one specific DOM
   structure and breaks silently when it changes.
**Why:** a `[class*='…']` override that worked yesterday breaks tomorrow when
the component adds a wrapper or renames an internal class — and you won't get a
type error, just a visually broken layout. Always start at the top of the
ladder; descend one rung only when the rung above has no handle.
---
## Color & shape
### Use semantic tokens, never raw hex or private tokens
❌ `color: #1677FF`
❌ `background: var(--g-color-private-blue-500)`
✓ `color: var(--g-color-text-link)`
✓ `background: var(--g-color-base-brand)`
**Why:** Gravity UI's color system is two-layered. The *private* layer
(`--g-color-private-<hue>-<step>`) is the raw palette — an implementation
detail that can change, never reference it directly. The *semantic* layer
(`--g-color-{group}-{role}`) encodes intent and is theme-aware. Use it:
- backgrounds/fills: `--g-color-base-*` (`base-background`, `base-brand`,
  `base-generic`, `base-danger-*`, …)
- text/icons: `--g-color-text-*` (`text-primary`, `text-secondary`, `text-hint`,
  `text-brand`, `text-link`, …)
- borders/lines: `--g-color-line-*` (`line-generic`, `line-brand`, `line-focus`,
  `line-danger`)
- effects: `--g-color-sfx-*` (`sfx-shadow`, `sfx-veil`, `sfx-fade`)
For text on a brand/colored background, use `--g-color-text-brand-contrast`
(not the plain brand color — it has no contrast guarantee).
### Border radius uses a token, never a hard-coded `px`
❌ `border-radius: 8px`
✓ `border-radius: var(--g-border-radius-m)`
**Why:** the scale is `--g-border-radius-{xs|s|m|l|xl}`. Components expose
their own radius variable on the same scale (`--g-button-border-radius`,
`--g-card-border-radius`, `--g-modal-border-radius`, …) so you can tune one
component without moving the global scale. Use a token, always.
---
## Component-prop traps (cross-cutting)
### `Button` uses `view`, not `variant` / `color`
❌ `<Button variant="primary">` / `<Button color="primary">`
✓ `<Button view="action">` (also `normal`, `outlined`, `flat`, `raised`;
   semantic `outlined-{info|success|warning|danger|utility|action}` and
   `flat-{secondary|info|success|warning|danger|utility|action}`; and
   `normal-contrast` / `outlined-contrast` / `flat-contrast` for colored
   backgrounds). There is no `special` or `clear` view.
### `Icon` takes an object via `data`, never a string name
❌ `<Icon name="check" />` / `<Icon data="Check" />`
✓ `<Icon data={CheckIcon} size={16} />`
**Why:** `Icon` (from `@gravity-ui/uikit`) is the *renderer*; the glyphs live
in `@gravity-ui/icons` as React components. There is no `name` prop. Pass the
imported component object through `data`. Never guess an icon name — use
`scripts/icon-image-search.sh` (reverse image search) or look it up at
`gravity-ui.com/icons`. See `references/icons.md`.
---
## When in doubt
1. Read `references/theming.md` (full token tables) and
   `references/layout.md` (spacing scale, breakpoints).
2. Read the chosen package's `dist/docs/INDEX.md` for component-specific props.
3. If still unsure, ask the user rather than guessing — invented APIs are the
   single biggest source of broken Gravity UI code.

  --g-color-text-link: #007AFF;
  --g-color-text-link-hover: #0066D6;
}
.g-root_theme_dark {
  /* different values — dark usually needs a brighter brand */
  --g-color-base-brand: #2E8BFF;
  /* … same set, dark-tuned … */
}
```
**Why:** the semantic layer has many tokens pointing at "brand" — selection,
focus, links, the contrast text on a brand background. Override only
`--g-color-base-brand` and you get a UI where the button is branded but
selection, links and focus rings are still the default accent. Provide the full
set, and provide it for *each* theme you support (dark themes usually need a
brighter brand than light). Forgetting `--g-color-text-brand-contrast` makes
text on a brand button unreadable.
Better than hand-writing: generate the full set with the
[Themer](https://gravity-ui.com/themer) web tool or
[`@gravity-ui/uikit-themer`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit-themer) — both
recalculate the dependent palette from a single base color.
### A section `ThemeProvider` with no provider above it themes the whole page
❌ **Incorrect** — a dark widget mounted where no `ThemeProvider` (or v8
`Provider`) wraps it: an embedded widget, a micro-frontend, a separate React
root:
```tsx
<ThemeProvider theme="dark">   {/* no provider above → writes to document.body */}
  <Toolbar />
</ThemeProvider>
```
✓ **Correct**:
```tsx
<ThemeProvider scoped theme="dark">
  <Toolbar />
</ThemeProvider>
```
**Why:** only the outermost `ThemeProvider` writes the theme class to
`document.body` — globally, last-wins. One nested inside another
`ThemeProvider` (or a v8 `Provider`) is always scoped, with or without the prop,
so a dark section inside the app needs no `scoped`. With no provider above,
`scoped` renders a dedicated `<div class="g-root g-root_theme_dark">` around the
children *and* updates the theme React context (so `useTheme` inside the
section sees the section's theme). For a CSS-only region without context, apply
the class manually: `<div className={getRootClassName({theme: 'dark'})}>`.
### Controls on a brand/colored background: fixed contrast, both themes
❌ **Incorrect** — default button on a brand-colored hero:
```tsx
<section style={{background: 'var(--g-color-base-brand)'}}>
  <Button>Sign up</Button>   {/* default view follows theme → low contrast on bright bg */}
</section>
```
✓ **Correct** — use a `*-contrast` view, which is built for a contrast
background, or scope a CSS override fixing contrast for both themes:
```tsx
<section style={{background: 'var(--g-color-base-brand)'}}>
  <Button view="normal-contrast">Sign up</Button>   {/* also outlined-contrast, flat-contrast */}
</section>
```
**Why:** a brand-colored fill is usually the *same* color in light and dark
(it's a fill, not a themed surface), so the control on top should keep a fixed
contrast in both themes rather than lightening/darkening with the theme.
`normal-contrast` / `outlined-contrast` / `flat-contrast` do exactly that.
Do **not** reach for `raised` here — its surface is themed (light in light,
dark in dark), so it does not hold contrast on a fixed fill. If no `*-contrast`
view fits, override the component's CSS API (`--g-button-background-color`,
`--g-button-text-color`, …) scoped to the section, with contrast values for
both themes. This is distinct from `--g-color-text-brand-contrast`, which is
about text on a *brand button* (`view="action"`).
### Customization ladder — descend only when there's no higher handle
When you need to change how a Gravity UI component looks, try in this order:
1. **Global tokens** (`--g-*` semantic tokens / theme) — change the look
   everywhere by changing the token, not components one by one.
2. **Component's own CSS API** (`--g-button-*`, `--g-card-border-radius`,
   `--g-text-input-*`, …) — scoped to the wrapper / class of the spot you're
   changing. Check the component's README for the variables it exposes.
3. **A narrow, flagged hack** — a custom class on a specific internal element,
   with a comment "hack on internal classes, pinned to version <X>", and a note
   to upstream it. Only after confirming step 1 and 2 don't expose a handle.
4. **NEVER** broad structural matches: `[class*='…']` or ID selectors against
   internal markup. Such an override is written against one specific DOM
   structure and breaks silently when it changes.
**Why:** a `[class*='…']` override that worked yesterday breaks tomorrow when
the component adds a wrapper or renames an internal class — and you won't get a
type error, just a visually broken layout. Always start at the top of the
ladder; descend one rung only when the rung above has no handle.
---
## Color & shape
### Use semantic tokens, never raw hex or private tokens
❌ `color: #1677FF`
❌ `background: var(--g-color-private-blue-500)`
✓ `color: var(--g-color-text-link)`
✓ `background: var(--g-color-base-brand)`
**Why:** Gravity UI's color system is two-layered. The *private* layer
(`--g-color-private-<hue>-<step>`) is the raw palette — an implementation
detail that can change, never reference it directly. The *semantic* layer
(`--g-color-{group}-{role}`) encodes intent and is theme-aware. Use it:
- backgrounds/fills: `--g-color-base-*` (`base-background`, `base-brand`,
  `base-generic`, `base-danger-*`, …)
- text/icons: `--g-color-text-*` (`text-primary`, `text-secondary`, `text-hint`,
  `text-brand`, `text-link`, …)
- borders/lines: `--g-color-line-*` (`line-generic`, `line-brand`, `line-focus`,
  `line-danger`)
- effects: `--g-color-sfx-*` (`sfx-shadow`, `sfx-veil`, `sfx-fade`)
For text on a brand/colored background, use `--g-color-text-brand-contrast`
(not the plain brand color — it has no contrast guarantee).
### Border radius uses a token, never a hard-coded `px`
❌ `border-radius: 8px`
✓ `border-radius: var(--g-border-radius-m)`
**Why:** the scale is `--g-border-radius-{xs|s|m|l|xl}`. Components expose
their own radius variable on the same scale (`--g-button-border-radius`,
`--g-card-border-radius`, `--g-modal-border-radius`, …) so you can tune one
component without moving the global scale. Use a token, always.
---
## Component-prop traps (cross-cutting)
### `Button` uses `view`, not `variant` / `color`
❌ `<Button variant="primary">` / `<Button color="primary">`
✓ `<Button view="action">` (also `normal`, `outlined`, `flat`, `raised`;
   semantic `outlined-{info|success|warning|danger|utility|action}` and
   `flat-{secondary|info|success|warning|danger|utility|action}`; and
   `normal-contrast` / `outlined-contrast` / `flat-contrast` for colored
   backgrounds). There is no `special` or `clear` view.
### `Icon` takes an object via `data`, never a string name
❌ `<Icon name="check" />` / `<Icon data="Check" />`
✓ `<Icon data={CheckIcon} size={16} />`
**Why:** `Icon` (from `@gravity-ui/uikit`) is the *renderer*; the glyphs live
in `@gravity-ui/icons` as React components. There is no `name` prop. Pass the
imported component object through `data`. Never guess an icon name — use
`scripts/icon-image-search.sh` (reverse image search) or look it up at
`gravity-ui.com/icons`. See `references/icons.md`.
---
## When in doubt
1. Read `references/theming.md` (full token tables) and
   `references/layout.md` (spacing scale, breakpoints).
2. Read the chosen package's `dist/docs/INDEX.md` for component-specific props.
3. If still unsure, ask the user rather than guessing — invented APIs are the
   single biggest source of broken Gravity UI code.

events.content:
Дашборд собран: 6 виджетов на сетке, которую можно двигать и менять по размеру. `tsc --noEmit` и `vite build` проходят, но в браузере я приложение не запускал, поэтому drag/resize и отрисовку графика не проверял.

**Что сделано**

- **Сетка:** `@gravity-ui/dashkit` (по таблице выбора в скилле для «дашборда из свободно расположенных виджетов»). Включается переключателем «Редактировать»: виджеты перетаскиваются и растягиваются, раскладка сохраняется в `localStorage`. Кнопка «Сбросить расположение» возвращает исходную.
- **Виджеты:** четыре KPI-карточки (выручка, заказы, новые клиенты, средний чек), график динамики выручки на `@gravity-ui/charts` и лента последних событий.
- **Язык:** интерфейс на русском через `configure({lang: Lang.Ru})`.

**Файлы**

- `src/App.tsx`: шапка с переключателем и сбросом, `DashKit`, сохранение раскладки.
- `src/dashboard/register.tsx`: настройки сетки и регистрация типов виджетов.
- `src/dashboard/widgets.tsx`: компоненты виджетов.
- `src/dashboard/config.ts`: раскладка по умолчанию, загрузка и сохранение с проверкой.
- `src/dashboard/types.ts`: типы виджетов, которые хранятся в раскладке.
- `src/dashboard/mockData.ts`: демо-данные, их нужно заменить на реальные.
- `package.json` и `package-lock.json`: добавлены `@gravity-ui/dashkit@10.5.2`, `@gravity-ui/charts@1.73.0`, `@gravity-ui/icons`.

**Решения, которые стоит проверить**

- **`@gravity-ui/charts` версии 1.73.0, а не 2.x.** Версия 2.x требует `@gravity-ui/uikit` ^8, а проект зафиксирован на 7.43.0. Я не стал обновлять uikit без вашего согласия.
- **Нет добавления и удаления виджетов из интерфейса.** Задача требовала только расположение. Для добавления нужен `ActionPanel` из dashkit; его можно добавить отдельно.
- **Данные демо-статичные.** Виджеты читают из `mockData.ts`, источника данных пока нет.

**Не проверено**

- Drag/resize и отрисовка в браузере, светлая и тёмная темы, узкий (~375px) и широкий (~1400px) экраны.
- При установке npm сообщил о 5 уязвимостях; я их не разбирал.

Изменения не закоммичены. Если нужно, могу запустить приложение и проверить перетаскивание и layout в браузере.
